descriptionChirho: A state of severe hardship, distress, or anguish, whether physical or emotional. All three sense clusters represent the same core meaning of matsoq with different grammatical frames: with conjunctive waw + preposition b- ('and-in-distress'), with conjunctive waw alone ('and-anguish'), or bare noun ('in-distress'). Uniformly attested across languages: English 'distress/anguish', Spanish 'angustia/afliccion', Hindi 'sankat (संकट)', Arabic 'diq (ضِيقٍ)/shidda (شِدَّةٌ)/da'iq (ضَائِقٍ)', Korean 'gotong (고통, pain)/gongung (곤궁, poverty)', Swahili 'dhiki/shida (hardship/trouble)'. No semantic distinction warrants separate senses.
